strategyReview: The system remains net profitable with a 63.4% overall win rate and realized PnL of +2.20. Weekend funding reversion longs continue to provide consistent, broad equity gains. One-touch NO edge live trades (4/4 wins, +$0.74) are promising but shadow tests on specific clusters (GOLD, BTC, ETH) have deteriorated, and several shadow-mined hypotheses are failing because they rely on large edge readings without trend or day-of-week context. Cross-asset confirmation (HYPE→BTC) is completely broken, and BTC IV expansion reversion is unreliable. PC-ratio signals are mildly profitable but asset-specific. The blocked shadow pipeline highlights high-return opportunities (USER_PM_IV_TOUCH_RICH_NO, WEEKEND_HL_FUNDING) that can be refined with stricter filters.

failureClusters.theme: Extreme edge readings lack bearish trend confirmation
failureClusters.evidence: H-534 gold one-touch NO edge (0/19) and H-001 BTC PM IV expansion (3/10 wins) both failed to produce >2% spot moves despite large edge/IV discount readings. Moves were often below threshold or reversed.
failureClusters.recommendation: Require a bearish trend filter (spot below 7d SMA, negative funding) for short theses to confirm directional pressure.

failureClusters.theme: Weekend funding reversion filters too permissive
failureClusters.evidence: H-539 CBRS (50% win) and H-537 AAPL (43% win) frequently failed when the entrance threshold was only -10% and the trigger occurred on weekdays; funding often whipsawed or remained negative without spot recovery.
failureClusters.recommendation: Enforce weekend-only (Sat/Sun) entry and deepen the funding threshold to < -20% to capture true overshoot episodes.

failureClusters.evidence: cross_asset_iv_compression_vol_expansion family (H-108 etc) recorded 0/9 scorable wins; HYPE spot above SMA and stable OI did not produce a >2% BTC long move in any test.
failureClusters.recommendation: Retire the thesis and avoid any long-BTC signals that rely solely on HYPE/meme asset confirmation.

failureClusters.theme: BTC listed-IV momentum long is weak
failureClusters.evidence: btc_listed_iv_momentum_confirmation long variants (H-012, H-170) achieved only 3/8 wins; the majority of long entries failed to exceed 2% and several stalled or declined.
failureClusters.recommendation: Require stronger spot momentum triggers (e.g., >2% daily gain) and confirm that IV expansion is accelerating rather than just positive.

newHypotheses.prediction: BTC spot will decline >2% within 7 days.

hypothesisReviews.observation: All 19 scorable tests failed to produce a >2% gold decline. The large underlying-cap edge on upside touch contracts did not translate into spot downside; gold remained rangebound or rallied. The core assumption that an edge alone predicts directional movement is invalid.
hypothesisReviews.invalidatedAssumption: A large underlying‑cap edge on gold one‑touch NO contracts reliably predicts a >2% spot decline within 2 days.

hypothesisReviews.observation: CBRS weekend funding reversion shadow tests showed frequent whipsaws and failures when funding was only moderately negative (-10%) and trigger occurred midweek. Funding normalisation often inverted without a sustained spot gain.
hypothesisReviews.invalidatedAssumption: Deeply negative CBRS funding reliably reverts and leads to a >2% spot gain within 2 days without additional extremity or reversal confirmation.

hypothesisReviews.observation: AAPL hypothesis failed when funding was around -10% and on non‑weekend days, with funding either staying negative or moving sideways. The idea that extreme negativity automatically snaps back is too broad.
hypothesisReviews.invalidatedAssumption: Extreme negative AAPL funding rapidly normalizes and leads to a >2% spot gain without requiring a true tail‑event overshoot.

hypothesisReviews.observation: BTC PM IV expansion reversion continued to underperform; 70% of tests failed to reach a 2% absolute move. The fixed IV thresholds (PM IV < 46, opt IV > 49) did not capture sufficient directional compression to guarantee a move, especially when overall trend context was ignored.
hypothesisReviews.invalidatedAssumption: BTC PM IV below 46 while options IV remains high guarantees a >2% absolute spot move within 3 days regardless of trend context.

hypothesisReviews.observation: Every test (9/9) for the cross-asset long-BTC signal failed, confirming HYPE momentum does not reliably predict BTC outperformance and the underlying cross-asset correlation thesis is broken.
hypothesisReviews.invalidatedAssumption: BTC above short‑term trend with HYPE spot above SMA and OI stable confirms a >2% BTC long move over 3‑7 days.

hypothesisReviews.observation: The long variant of BTC listed-IV momentum only produced 3 wins in 8 tests; many entries stalled or reversed. Spot gain with positive IV change is insufficient to guarantee a 2% follow‑through.
hypothesisReviews.invalidatedAssumption: BTC spot gaining vs short-term trend with positive IV change yields >2% further gain within 3-7 days.

journalEntry: Tonight's review focused on diagnosing failing shadow hypotheses. Gold one-touch edge (H-534) and BTC PM IV expansion (H-001) both collapsed because extreme readings alone do not guarantee directional follow-through; they now require trend filters. Weekend funding shadows for CBRS and AAPL were too generous—tightening the threshold to -20% and enforcing weekend day-of-week should rescue the thesis. Cross-asset HYPE→BTC long is conclusively broken, and BTC listed-IV momentum long is weak; both enter the invalidAssumption ledger so future runs do not resurrect them. Meanwhile, the FIND mining results present high-potential patterns: informed flow fading (dumb money highs), extreme PC-ratio shorts on GOLD with a trend filter, and one-touch NO edge buckets with moderate edge strength (3-8 pts). Seven new FIND-authored hypotheses and four focused refinements were proposed, all using catalog-validated keys. No parameter adjustments were made as current signal risk settings appear adequate for live strategies; the primary work is improving hypothesis quality to raise the forward test win rate.
